actions.text: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.

dimensions.assessment: Affects members of the Armed Forces deployed in combat zones, military medical personnel, and eligible entities developing diagnostic technologies.
dimensions.evidence: diagnosis of traumatic brain injuries among members of the Armed Forces in connection with operational deployments, including in combat zones

dimensions.assessment: Aims to improve medical readiness, treatment accuracy, and long-term prognoses for military members suffering from traumatic brain injuries.
dimensions.evidence: enhance the health, survival, and long-term prognosis of members of the Armed Forces; and (D) how such technologies may improve military readiness

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes an appropriation of $5,000,000 annually for fiscal years 2026 through 2029 to carry out the pilot program and grants.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated $5,000,000 to the Secretary of Defense for each of fiscal years 2026 through 2029 to carry out this section.

dimensions.assessment: Creates a targeted pilot program and grant mechanism within the Department of Defense rather than a sweeping restructuring of military health care.
dimensions.evidence: direct the Secretary of Defense to establish a pilot program to facilitate the development of certain traumatic brain injury diagnostics

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a temporary pilot program with a defined authorization spanning fiscal years 2026 through 2029, terminating on September 30, 2029.
dimensions.evidence: The authority to carry out the program shall terminate on September 30, 2029.

missing_information: The specific number of grants to be awarded and the individual grant amounts.
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a 4-year pilot program with $5 million authorized annually to facilitate the development and evaluation of traumatic brain injury diagnostics for members of the Armed Forces.
